title: Mind-Bending Experiences - All Things Product Podcast with Teresa Torres & Petra Wille
text: Mind-Bending Experiences - All Things Product Podcast with Teresa Torres & Petra Wille Our Courses Train Your Team Articles Just Now Possible Get in Touch Sign in Subscribe Mind-Bending Experiences - All Things Product Podcast with Teresa Torres & Petra Wille Teresa Torres 20 Oct 2026 13 min Listen to this episode on: Spotify | Apple Podcasts Team events are making a comeback. After years of remote work and tight budgets, companies are bringing people together again, and many are looking for experiences that go beyond the usual offsite. So should companies deliberately send their people somewhere strange, uncomfortable, and awe-inspiring, and what actually happens to a team when they do? Petra Wille and Teresa Torres trade stories about the experiences that quietly rewired how they see the world. Petra shares the art-like, genre-bending conferences she attends for "new lenses and new angles," while Teresa recounts the World Domination Summit — and the "one year from now" exercise that led her to pack up and move to Oregon. From there they get into why awe and being fully in the moment matter, drawing on kite surfing, mountain biking, hockey, and a Formula One track day, and why learning a new sport quietly teaches you to be a beginner again. But the heart of the episode is a caution: comfort-zone-pushing experiences only work when leaders co-design them with their teams. Push too far, and you alienate people instead of growing them. Key Takeaways The experiences that shake us most are often raw, human stories about people finding what's meaningful to them — not polished tales of achievement. "Mind-bending" experiences work like art: you come back enriched even when the ideas don't obviously apply to your corner of the world. A sport that demands 100% of your attention is a rare, restorative escape — and that presence can spark the very energy leaders hope will lead to innovation. Learning a new sport lets people practice being a beginner again: getting comfortable with continuous improvement and with being outside their comfort zone. Stretch people only within the "zone of proximity" — close enough to what they know to grow them, not so far it alienates. Leaders should co-design these experiences with their teams, creating a safe way to surface abilities, disabilities, and comfort levels before planning anything. Mind the room: hierarchy, politics, and cultural norms shape whether people feel safe struggling in front of colleagues. Notable Moments "A word that comes to mind is awe. It's such a little word that has so much power." — Teresa "You go there for new lenses, new angles — thoughts you have never thought." — Petra "I actually moved to Oregon because of this conference." — Teresa "You cannot practice that while checking your email." — Petra "When you push people outside their comfort zone, it has to be in the zone of proximity. If you push too far, it's not helpful." — Teresa Resources & Links: Follow Teresa Torres: https://ProductTalk.org Follow Petra Wille: https://Petra-Wille.com Mentioned in this episode: House of Beautiful Business — the immersive, genre-bending conference Petra attends (plus a similarly-minded conference she used to attend in Malmö, Sweden) World Domination Summit — Chris Guillebeau 's conference, tagline "how to live a remarkable life in a conventional world" Colin O'Brady — the adventurer Teresa half-recalls as "Colin," known for the first solo, unsupported crossing of Antarctica (memoir The Impossible First ); fittingly, he's based in Portland — the city Teresa moved to The Comfort Crisis by Michael Easter — recommended reading on discomfort and meaning Join the Conversation: Have thoughts on this episode?
